chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Listening to singing and vanities grows hypocrisy in the heart just as water grows the crop.

key_terms.اللَّهْوِ: Frivolous entertainment or diversion that distracts from God
key_terms.النِّفَاقَ: Hypocrisy or duality of heart, where inner belief contradicts outer action
key_terms.الْغِنَاءِ: Singing or melodic recitation, often distinguished from simple speech
key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: The spiritual center of understanding and faith, not just the physical organ

ai.seo_question: How does listening to music affect the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the auditory consumption of *ghina'* (melodious singing) and *lahw* (frivolous entertainment) actively cultivates *nifaq* (hypocrisy) within the heart, likening this spiritual growth to water nurturing crops. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is not merely a moral warning but a metaphysical claim that such sounds corrupt the inner essence, creating a duality between outward appearance and inner reality. This hadith is foundational in establishing the jurisprudential basis for prohibiting *ghina'* as a means of preserving spiritual integrity and sincerity (*ikhlas*).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Listening to the singing (music) and the vanities grow the hypocrisy in the heart just as the water grows the plantation’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Anbasah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Listening to al-Ghina’ (music (and singing)) and useless things grows hypocrisy just as water grows green plants.’”
